## Purpose

This SOP describes the estimation of soil organic matter (SOM) content
using the loss-on-ignition (LOI) method. SOM is quantified by measuring
the mass lost when oven-dried soil is combusted at 550 °C in a muffle
furnace [@heiri2001; @Nelson1996].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved soil samples collected per
  [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling and Processing](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd).
- **Does not apply to:** Soils with high calcium carbonate content
  (CaCO~3~ decomposes above ~450 °C and may inflate LOI values; consider
  an alternative method such as elemental analysis for calcareous soils
  [@heiri2001]).
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133.


## Definitions

- **Ash-free dry mass (AFDM):** The mass remaining after removing water
  (drying at 105 °C) and organic matter (igniting at 550 °C); equivalent
  to the inorganic mineral mass of the sample.
- **Crucible:** A heat-resistant porcelain or ceramic container used to
  hold soil samples during furnace ignition; must be pre-ignited and
  weighed to constant mass before use.
- **Inorganic carbon (IC):** Carbon associated with carbonates
  (CaCO~3~, MgCO~3~); released as CO~2~ during ignition above ~550 °C;
  can inflate LOI values in calcareous soils if ignition temperature is
  not controlled or if acid pre-treatment is omitted [@heiri2001].
- **Loss on ignition (LOI):** The percentage mass loss when an
  oven-dried soil is ignited at 550 °C for 4 hours:
  $LOI = (M_{105} - M_{550}) / M_{105} \times 100$; used as a proxy
  for SOM content [@heiri2001].
- **Soil organic matter (SOM):** The organic fraction of soil,
  including plant and animal residues at various stages of decomposition,
  microbial biomass, and stabilized humus; estimated by LOI as
  approximately $\text{SOM} \approx 1.72 \times \text{LOI}$ (the Van
  Bemmelen factor) when organic carbon is the target [@Nelson1996].
- **Tare mass:** The pre-weighed mass of the empty, pre-ignited
  crucible; subtracted from all subsequent measurements to obtain
  sample mass.
- **Van Bemmelen factor:** The empirical conversion factor (1.724)
  relating organic carbon content to SOM by assuming that SOM contains
  58% carbon by mass; use with caution for soils with unusual organic
  matter composition [@Nelson1996].

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |

| Trained Personnel | Perform analysis, record and report results             |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Thermal:** Muffle furnace operates at 550 °C; severe burn risk.
  Drying oven operates at 105 °C. Ceramic crucibles remain extremely
  hot for many minutes after removal from the furnace.
- **Physical:** Crucible tongs can slip; always use two hands when
  moving hot crucibles.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Laboratory coat
- [ ] Heat-resistant gloves (mandatory when handling furnace-hot
      crucibles)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
and [SOP-L111 Muffle Furnace](SOP-L111-muffle-furnace.qmd). For burns,
cool with running water for at least 10 minutes and seek medical
attention.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item               | Notes                                              |
|:-------------------|:---------------------------------------------------|
| Muffle furnace     | Capable of 550 ±10 °C; programmable ramp preferred |
| Drying oven        | Regulated at 105 ±2 °C                            |
| Analytical balance | Resolution ≥ 0.0001 g (0.1 mg)                    |
| Desiccator         | With active color-indicating silica gel            |
| Crucible tongs     | Heat-resistant; long-handled                       |

### Consumables

| Item                    | Notes                                       |
|:------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Porcelain or ceramic crucibles | Pre-ignited to constant mass        |
| Weighing paper or spatulas | For soil transfer                         |


## Procedure

### Crucible Preparation

1. Pre-ignite crucibles in the muffle furnace at 550 °C for at least
   1 hour to remove any residual organic matter.
2. Transfer to a desiccator and cool to room temperature.
3. Weigh each crucible to the nearest 0.0001 g and record as the tare
   mass ($W_{\text{crucible}}$).

### Oven Drying at 105 °C

1. Using a spatula, transfer 5--10 g of air-dried, sieved soil into a
   pre-weighed crucible.
2. Record the mass of crucible plus moist or air-dry soil.
3. Place uncovered crucibles in the drying oven at 105 °C for at least
   24 hours.
4. Transfer crucibles to a desiccator and cool to room temperature
   (approximately 20--30 minutes).
5. Weigh to the nearest 0.0001 g and record as $W_{\text{105}}$ (mass
   of oven-dried soil only, i.e., crucible + dry soil mass minus crucible
   tare).

### Combustion at 550 °C

1. Transfer the crucibles containing oven-dried soil directly into the
   muffle furnace [@heiri2001].
2. Ramp the furnace to 550 °C (if programmable, use a ramp rate of
   approximately 10 °C per minute to prevent crucible cracking and
   reduce convective loss of fine particles).
3. Hold at 550 °C for 4 hours [@heiri2001].
4. Turn off the furnace and allow crucibles to cool inside the furnace
   until they can be safely transferred (below approximately 200 °C).
5. Transfer crucibles to a desiccator and cool to room temperature.
6. Weigh to the nearest 0.0001 g and record as $W_{\text{550}}$ (mass
   of combusted soil, excluding crucible).

### Calculation

Soil organic matter content is calculated as [@heiri2001]:

$$
\text{SOM (\%)} = \left( \frac{W_{105} - W_{550}}{W_{105}} \right) \times 100
$$

where:

- $W_{105}$ = mass of oven-dried soil (g)
- $W_{550}$ = mass of soil after combustion at 550 °C (g)

To convert LOI (%) to approximate organic carbon (%OC), divide by
1.724 (the Van Bemmelen factor); note that this conversion assumes
constant elemental composition and is less accurate for samples with
unusual organic matter [@Nelson1996].


## Quality Control

- Run analytical duplicates for at least 10% of samples; coefficient
  of variation between duplicates should be less than 5%
  [@heiri2001].
- Include an empty crucible blank in each furnace run to verify no
  mass gain from ambient contamination.
- Include a laboratory reference soil with known SOM content in each
  batch.
- Verify oven (105 °C) and furnace (550 °C) temperatures using a
  calibrated thermocouple at regular intervals.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Disposal Method                             |
|:------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Combusted soil residue  | Standard trash (inert mineral ash)          |
| Crucibles               | Clean and reuse                             |

## Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L111 Muffle Furnace](SOP-L111-muffle-furnace.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate safe operation of the muffle furnace and drying oven
4. Demonstrate proper use of the analytical balance and desiccator
5. Perform the procedure under supervision with acceptable duplicate
   precision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
